scope: The five Training & local catalog entries, their training and inference modes, and committed publication-selected evidence. Source inspection and provider-free wrapper probes only; no new training, inference or provider calls.
native_structure_definition: False means the inspected question paths do not preserve native object/array/null instructions and rich criterion entries. JSON state, string-valued Choice maps and Score lists, and JSON serialized into prompt text are separate capabilities. It does not measure model quality.

records.title: Prompt evolution
records.input: BANKING77 customer messages restricted to ten fixed intent labels. Ten independent records share a state object; each question names its record. Full run uses 50 reflection-training, 20 validation and 50 final held-out records.

questions.primitives: 10 independent Choices over the shared record map

records.instructions_and_criteria: String instruction plus fixed string intent descriptions. Random mutation, hill climbing, OPRO and GEPA change the instruction; GEPA's candidate has only an instruction component. No structured criterion optimization or Jev weight update occurs.
records.distribution_use: Evaluation rows retain Choice probabilities and confidence. Search fitness is exact-label accuracy, not NLL, Brier or distribution matching. GEPA receives record-level outputs and correctness feedback; final test labels do not enter reflection.
records.output_effect: Freezes one prompt per method using validation, then evaluates held-out tasks. The browser displays recorded candidate cards and test statistics; it does not run an optimizer.
execution_modes: OPRO with a generative proposal model
Real GEPA adapter with a generative reflection model
records.recorded_evidence: Committed full-run records show held-out accuracy 0.86 for unchanged, random, hill climb and GEPA; OPRO is 0.84. The evaluation ceiling is 250 classified records per search, with 240 actual calls for the three non-GEPA searches and 250 for GEPA. This ten-label derivative does not establish a general prompt-optimization gain.
records.depth_opportunity: Extend this experiment with a new frozen comparison of string instructions, equivalent JSON-as-text and native structured instructions/criteria. Separate instruction and criterion search components; select on validation with a declared distribution-sensitive objective and include reflection cost. Preserve the existing run and completed local readout study.

records.title: Active labeling
records.input: A deterministic fictional drink menu, 160 authored training-pool requests and 80 held-out request templates. Random and student-uncertainty acquisition start with the same eight examples and receive 32 attempted labels each in the full run.
records.instructions_and_criteria: The menu and numbered requests are structured state. Choice instructions are prose, and each option's menu facts become Python str(dict), not native structured criterion values. The policy never rewrites these questions.
records.distribution_use: Full teacher answers are cached and published, including probabilities when supplied. Logistic regression trains on only the selected teacher label. Uncertainty acquisition uses the student's 1 minus maximum predicted probability, not teacher confidence. Teacher distributions do not become soft targets.
records.output_effect: Actual local TF-IDF logistic-regression weights are fitted and exported. Browser inspection shows learning curves and teacher-labeled examples; it does not fit or invoke the student interactively.
execution_modes: Random acquisition with local logistic-regression fitting
Student-uncertainty acquisition with local logistic-regression fitting
records.recorded_evidence: 51 unique teacher labels served both methods. At 32 attempted labels, random reaches 0.5375 test accuracy and uncertainty acquisition 0.525 on 80 authored cases. Recorded teacher labels agree with the menu oracle; that does not establish broader annotation quality.
records.depth_opportunity: Compare hard labels with full-distribution distillation and a validation-fixed defer policy on ambiguous requests. Preserve attempted-label and cost budgets, use independent menu semantics for correctness, and test acquisition on a more varied frozen request set. Native menu criteria require the wrapper foundations change first.

records.title: Learning from rewards
records.input: Authored drink requests and the complete fictional menu. The full recipe attempts to annotate 48 training requests and evaluates on 80 independently labeled held-out requests.

questions.primitives: 1 Noul for satisfying all explicit requirements

records.instructions_and_criteria: Structured menu/request state, one prose Noul per candidate. The entire compatibility rule is in the instruction; there are no explicit true/false criteria and no separate per-requirement questions.
records.distribution_use: Continuous probability of compatibility becomes the reward for that candidate. All candidate rewards are available, so the update computes the exact gradient of expected reward under the local softmax policy. Independent oracle accuracy is measured separately from teacher reward.
records.output_effect: Updates and exports real linear TF-IDF policy weights over 240 fixed steps. It is full-information contextual-bandit optimization, not sampled RL or language-model RLHF. The test curve does not choose a checkpoint.
execution_modes: Hosted Noul reward annotation for every menu candidate
Local linear-policy optimization with a full reward vector
records.recorded_evidence: The committed run has 44 successfully annotated training requests, 80 test cases and 576 nonzero policy parameters. At step 240, mean training reward is 0.7973929 and independent test accuracy is 0.6375. The two metrics have different meanings.
records.depth_opportunity: Freeze a decomposed checklist and compare its code-defined aggregation with the existing single compatibility question. Add counterexamples that earn high predicted reward but violate a menu requirement; measure independent correctness and reward calibration. Any changed reward or structured rubric belongs to a new condition, not the recorded pilot.

records.title: SmolLM decision model
records.input: BANKING77 messages transformed into four-candidate intent selection, a yes/no query about one intent and a three-level relevance rubric. Gold labels come from the dataset, not Jev distillation.

questions.primitives: 1 four-option Choice + 1 Noul + 1 three-level Score derivative

questions.scope: hosted Jev reference per test example

records.instructions_and_criteria: Custom string instruction and option-list format. A shared document prefix and branch attention mask isolate questions. Only endpoint Score labels are generated; no gold example trains the middle level. This is an architecture-transfer pilot attributed to Kev, not its full recipe.
records.distribution_use: Learns option/query projections and rank-four LoRA updates in upper SmolLM2 attention layers using cross-entropy over all three tasks. Full probability vectors support accuracy and Brier evaluation. Checkpoint selection uses validation Choice accuracy only. Saved inference returns choice plus option-keyed probabilities for every question, without primitive-specific Score means or Noul fields.
records.output_effect: Actual parameter updates and saved inference weights. The browser displays recorded before/after metrics. Local CLI inference is a separate Python path, not the roadmap decision wire contract.
execution_modes: Frozen-base initialization with trainable projections and LoRA
240-step supervised parameter adaptation in the full recipe
records.recorded_evidence: Across 77 test records, Choice accuracy rises from 0.3246753 to 0.6623377; Noul stays at 0.4025974 while its Brier worsens; Score endpoint accuracy rises from 0.3376623 to 0.4545455. Four-candidate results are not original 77-label BANKING77 scores. Packing rejects documents above 160 tokens; saved inference also caps the whole packed request at 2048 tokens, 16 questions and 32 options.
records.depth_opportunity: Evaluate intermediate Score targets, full-distribution calibration and order sensitivity with a newly frozen protocol. Preserve descriptive criteria and typed output semantics in an explicit adapter, and measure all three primitives before implying native parity. Do not merge this LoRA pilot with the later frozen-readout study.
